text_blocks.snippet: Treatment for type 2 diabetes focuses on keeping blood sugar levels in a healthy range, protecting organs, and managing related health conditions like high blood pressure or high cholesterol.
snippet_highlighted_words: keeping blood sugar levels in a healthy range, protecting organs, and managing related health conditions like high blood pressure or high cholesterol

list.snippet: Healthy Eating: Focus on lean proteins, non-starchy vegetables, complex carbohydrates, and good fats while limiting excess sugars and refined starches.
Physical Activity: Aim for regular movement, such as 150 minutes of moderate-intensity aerobic exercise per week, plus muscle-strengthening workouts.
Weight Management: Losing even 5% to 10% of your body weight can significantly improve how your body handles insulin and regulates blood sugar.

text_blocks.snippet: If lifestyle changes are not enough to reach target glucose levels, healthcare providers typically prescribe pills taken by mouth. The American Diabetes Association provides detailed guides on these medications: American Diabetes Association +2

list.snippet: Metformin: Most often the first medicine prescribed; it lowers glucose production in the liver and helps the body use insulin better.
Sulfonylureas: Examples include glipizide and glimepiride; they stimulate the pancreas to make more insulin.
Thiazolidinediones (TZDs): Examples include pioglitazone (Actos); they help insulin work better in fat and muscle tissue.
DPP-4 Inhibitors (Gliptins): They block an enzyme to help enhance the body's natural blood-sugar-lowering hormones.
SGLT2 Inhibitors: They help the kidneys remove excess glucose from the body through urine.

GLP-1 Receptor Agonists & Dual GLP-1/GIP Agonists: These are injectable medications that boost insulin secretion during meals, slow digestion, promote fullness, and can support weight loss and heart health.

If the body stops producing enough natural insulin over time, or if other medications are not enough, doctors may prescribe insulin therapy via injections or an insulin pump. Options include long-acting (basal) and short-acting (mealtime) insulins.
Blood Glucose Tracking: Using a home blood glucose meter or a continuous glucose monitor (CGM) helps track how food, activity, and medicine affect your body.

Weight Loss (Bariatric) Surgery: For individuals with severe obesity and difficult-to-manage type 2 diabetes, metabolic or weight-loss surgery can be a very effective option to improve or even remit the condition.

text_blocks.snippet: You can learn more via the National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases overview of treatments.
